newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares finish lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares finish lower in dull trade.

text.p: Indian shares ended lower at major stock exchanges on Thursday amidst a lack of market-moving news, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 15.83 points, or 0.51 percent, lower at 3,110.23, off 3,134.14.
"The market seems to be in a state of inertia....there is hardly any major activity," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive at Bombay-based Lloyds Securities, a local brokerage.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index dropped 7.45 points, or 0.83 percent, to close at 889.39.
ITC closed 0.50 rupees lower at 263.50 at the BSE after rising to 271.0 in mid-session, with 2.60 million shares traded.
Indian financial institutions and B.A.T Industries Plc, major shareholders of ITC, will review operations of the tobacco giant at a board meeting on Friday.
Last month, a federal agency arrested several senior ITC officials including two former chairmen for allegedly violating India's foreign exchange rules.
On Tuesday, an Indian court rejected the bail plea of the two former chairmen and remanded them to judicial custody until November 26.
"The market was unable to maintain higher levels as profit-takers preferred to book profits at every rise," said Vikas Puri of Delhi-based Puri Financial Portfolios.
SBI lost 3.0 rupees to 219.75 rupees, TISCO 1.75 to 166.75, Reliance 1.0 to 184.50, ACC 42.70 to 1,363.0, TELCO 11.00 to 405.50 and Bajaj Auto 3.0 to 942.25.
Hind Lever rose 10.70 to 805.0, Indian Hotels 14.7 to 670.0 and BHEL 2.50 to 185.75.
